es: Reconocer pares de vocabulario británico y estadounidense y palabras de otras variedades (Australia, India, Irlanda) con su significado.

teaching.en: In Britain a lift is what a colleague from Boston would call an elevator, yet British and American speakers remain mutually intelligible, and neither word is more correct.
teaching.es: En Gran Bretaña un «lift» es lo que un colega de Boston llamaría «elevator», pero los hablantes británicos y estadounidenses se entienden entre sí, y ninguna palabra es más correcta.
teaching.explanationEs: Lift (RU) y elevator (EE. UU.) significan «ascensor»; mutually intelligible = se entienden mutuamente.
segments: In Britain a lift is what a colleague from Boston would call an elevator,
yet British and American speakers remain mutually intelligible, and neither word is more correct.
teaching.audioText: In Britain a lift is what a colleague from Boston would call an elevator, yet British and American speakers remain mutually intelligible, and neither word is more correct.

teaching.en: Our landlord promised that the flat would be quiet, yet a lorry still parks on the pavement every morning, which an American would describe as a truck on the sidewalk.
teaching.es: Nuestro propietario prometió que el apartamento sería tranquilo, pero cada mañana sigue estacionando un camión en la acera, que un estadounidense describiría como «a truck on the sidewalk».
teaching.explanationEs: Flat, lorry y pavement son británicos; en EE. UU. se dice apartment, truck y sidewalk (y pavement allí es el asfalto de la calzada).
segments: Our landlord promised that the flat would be quiet, yet a lorry still parks on
the pavement every morning, which an American would describe as a truck on the sidewalk.
teaching.audioText: Our landlord promised that the flat would be quiet, yet a lorry still parks on the pavement every morning, which an American would describe as a truck on the sidewalk.

teaching.en: After standing in the queue for twenty minutes, we finally ordered tea and a biscuit, although an American biscuit is a soft bread roll usually eaten with a meal, not a sweet snack.
teaching.es: Tras veinte minutos en la fila, por fin pedimos té y una galleta, aunque un «biscuit» estadounidense es un panecillo blando que suele comerse con una comida, no un dulce.
teaching.explanationEs: Queue y biscuit son británicos (line y cookie en EE. UU.); biscuit es un falso amigo entre variedades.
segments: After standing in the queue for twenty minutes, we finally ordered tea and a biscuit, although an
American biscuit is a soft bread roll usually eaten with a meal, not a sweet snack.
teaching.audioText: After standing in the queue for twenty minutes, we finally ordered tea and a biscuit, although an American biscuit is a soft bread roll usually eaten with a meal, not a sweet snack.

teaching.en: My Australian colleague promised to call me this arvo, and he ended his message with mate, which sounds warm and relaxed in Sydney rather than rude.
teaching.es: Mi colega australiano prometió llamarme esta tarde y cerró su mensaje con «mate», que en Sídney suena cercano y relajado, no maleducado.
teaching.explanationEs: Arvo es la forma australiana abreviada de afternoon; mate es un apelativo amistoso muy frecuente.
segments: My Australian colleague promised to call me this arvo, and he ended his
message with mate, which sounds warm and relaxed in Sydney rather than rude.
teaching.audioText: My Australian colleague promised to call me this arvo, and he ended his message with mate, which sounds warm and relaxed in Sydney rather than rude.

teaching.en: Irish speakers ask about the craic when they want to know how a night out went, and in India a salary of six lakh means six hundred thousand rupees a year.
teaching.es: Los irlandeses preguntan por el «craic» cuando quieren saber cómo fue una salida nocturna, y en India un sueldo de seis «lakh» son seiscientas mil rupias al año.
teaching.explanationEs: Craic (irlandés) = diversión, buen ambiente; lakh (India) = 100 000.
segments: Irish speakers ask about the craic when they want to know how a night out went,
and in India a salary of six lakh means six hundred thousand rupees a year.
teaching.audioText: Irish speakers ask about the craic when they want to know how a night out went, and in India a salary of six lakh means six hundred thousand rupees a year.

teaching.en: Linguists treat every regional dialect as a complete system rather than a mistake, yet a single word can give away where a speaker grew up.
teaching.es: Los lingüistas tratan cada dialecto regional como un sistema completo y no como un error, pero una sola palabra puede delatar dónde creció un hablante.
teaching.explanationEs: Give away (+ where/who) = dejar ver un dato sin querer, como el origen de alguien.
segments: Linguists treat every regional dialect as a complete system rather than a mistake,
yet a single word can give away where a speaker grew up.
teaching.audioText: Linguists treat every regional dialect as a complete system rather than a mistake, yet a single word can give away where a speaker grew up.

prompt.es: Elige cómo reescribir el correo del propietario para un lector de Boston.

choices.text: The flat has an elevator, and there is always a queue at the bus stop on Mondays.
The apartment has an elevator, and there is always a line at the bus stop on Mondays.
The apartment has a lift, and there is always a line at the bus stop on Mondays.

feedback.es: Para un lector de EE. UU. hay que cambiar las tres palabras británicas: apartment, elevator y line.

hint.es: Cambia las tres palabras británicas: flat, lift y queue.

origin.text: Landlord's email: 'The flat has a lift, and there is always a queue at the bus stop on Monday mornings, so please leave early.'

prompt.es: Completa con la palabra irlandesa: «El ambiente fue genial.»

answer.text: craic
accepted: craic

feedback.es: Craic es la palabra irlandesa para la diversión y el buen ambiente de un rato con amigos.

hint.es: Es la palabra irlandesa de la lista, la que empieza por cr.

origin.text: Tom, who is from Cork, described his weekend: 'The match was poor, but the ___ afterwards at the party was great.'

prompt.es: Ordena: «El camión se detuvo junto a la acera frente a nuestro apartamento.»

answer.text: The lorry stopped beside the pavement outside our flat

feedback.es: Stopped beside the pavement sitúa al camión, y outside our flat indica dónde: las dos palabras regionales son británicas.

hint.es: Empieza por The lorry y termina con el apartamento.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada palabra regional con su significado y su variedad.

feedback.es: Cada palabra nace en una variedad distinta: pavement y queue en Gran Bretaña, arvo en Australia, lakh en India y craic en Irlanda.

prompt.es: Escucha a la narradora y elige qué le pasaba con el ingeniero indio.

choices.text: He complained that she earned less than he did.
He refused to tell her how much his job paid.
He gave figures in a unit she did not recognise.

feedback.es: Él daba su sueldo en lakh, una unidad que ella no conocía; no hay queja ni negativa a hablar de dinero.

origin.audio: Last year I shared a flat with a girl from Cork and an engineer from Pune. She was always asking whether the craic had been good, while he quoted his salary in lakh and could not see why I needed an explanation. Between the two of them I learned more about English than in any classroom, and I still smile whenever somebody mentions a lakh.

prompt.es: Escribe en inglés americano: «El camión bloquea la acera junto al ascensor.»

answer.text: The truck is blocking the sidewalk next to the elevator.
accepted: The truck is blocking the sidewalk next to the elevator.
The truck is blocking the sidewalk beside the elevator.
The truck is blocking the sidewalk by the elevator.
The truck is blocking the sidewalk near the elevator.
The truck is blocking the sidewalk close to the elevator.
The truck blocks the sidewalk next to the elevator.
The truck blocks the sidewalk beside the elevator.
The truck blocks the sidewalk by the elevator.
The truck blocks the sidewalk near the elevator.
The truck blocks the sidewalk close to the elevator.
A truck is blocking the sidewalk next to the elevator.
A truck is blocking the sidewalk beside the elevator.
A truck is blocking the sidewalk by the elevator.
A truck is blocking the sidewalk near the elevator.
A truck is blocking the sidewalk close to the elevator.
A truck blocks the sidewalk next to the elevator.
A truck blocks the sidewalk beside the elevator.
A truck blocks the sidewalk by the elevator.
A truck blocks the sidewalk near the elevator.
A truck blocks the sidewalk close to the elevator.

feedback.es: En inglés americano se dice truck, sidewalk y elevator, no lorry, pavement ni lift.

origin.text: El camión bloquea la acera junto al ascensor.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué hizo el primo estadounidense el primer día.

choices.text: He asked for an elevator and heard the local word.
He waited at the bakery for a biscuit and called the baker mate.
He laughed at my dad for using the word lift.

feedback.es: Preguntó por el elevator y el padre de quien narra le dijo que allí se llama lift; lo de la panadería ocurre al final de la semana y quien se ríe es el padre, no él.

origin.audio: My American cousin spent a month with us in Leeds, and he kept a list of words that confused him. On his first morning he asked where the elevator was, and my dad laughed and said we call it a lift. By the end of the week he was waiting outside the bakery for a biscuit, calling the baker mate, and joking that nobody back home would believe him.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué actitud muestra el primo ante las palabras nuevas.

choices.text: He feels irritated that people in Leeds will not use American words.
He enjoys the differences and expects to tell his friends about them.
He worries that his friends will think he has changed his accent.

feedback.es: Bromea con que nadie en casa le creerá: se divierte con las diferencias, no le molestan ni le preocupan.

origin.audio: My American cousin spent a month with us in Leeds, and he kept a list of words that confused him. On his first morning he asked where the elevator was, and my dad laughed and said we call it a lift. By the end of the week he was waiting outside the bakery for a biscuit, calling the baker mate, and joking that nobody back home would believe him.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cuidó su acento por meses, pero una palabra la delató.»

answer.text: away
accepted: away

feedback.es: Give away también admite un objeto: gave her away significa que una palabra dejó ver su origen sin que ella quisiera.

origin.text: She had worked on her accent for months, but in the end one single word gave her ___.

prompt.es: Lee el correo de Sídney. ¿Qué transmite el uso de «mate» en él?

choices.text: A cautious tone, because he is unsure how to address an American manager.
A rude attitude to a more important person.
A friendly, informal tone that is still polite.

feedback.es: En el inglés australiano mate es un apelativo amistoso; el resto del correo es cordial y sin prisa, sin rastro de nervios ni de mala educación.

origin.text: Email from Sydney to a new American manager: 'Thanks for sending the plan, mate. Could we talk this arvo? There is no rush on the report, and I will have it ready by Friday.'

prompt.es: Lee el correo. ¿Con qué propósito añade el autor la cifra completa?

choices.text: To help readers from other countries understand the amount.
To correct a mistake he made in the first figure.
To suggest that nobody should use the word lakh.

feedback.es: Añade seiscientas mil rupias porque lakh puede no ser entendido fuera de India: busca evitar un malentendido.

origin.text: From an email: 'Dear Mr Rao, the salary we can offer is six lakh a year. I realise that this figure may look strange to our American colleagues, so I have written the amount in full, six hundred thousand rupees, at the end of the page.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Por favor, ponte al final de la fila y espera tu turno.»

answer.text: queue
accepted: queue

feedback.es: Un oficial británico dice queue; en EE. UU. se diría line.

origin.text: At the airport, a British officer noticed that a tourist was not waiting for his turn. Politely, he said: 'Excuse me, please join the end of the ___ and wait your turn.'

prompt.es: Ordena: «El ambiente fue tan bueno que nadie quiso irse temprano.»

answer.text: The craic was so good that nobody wanted to leave early

feedback.es: So good that + oración expresa el resultado: craic es el sujeto y nobody wanted to leave early, la consecuencia.

es: Reconocer y usar variantes de ortografía y gramática británicas y estadounidenses (colour/color, gotten/got, at/on the weekend).

teaching.en: In American English you might say that the situation has gotten worse, whereas a British speaker would say that it has got worse.
teaching.es: En inglés americano podrías decir que la situación «has gotten worse», mientras que un británico diría «has got worse».
teaching.explanationEs: Gotten es el participio estadounidense de get con sentido de «volverse» o «conseguir»; el británico usa got.
segments: In American English you might say that the situation has gotten worse,
whereas a British speaker would say that it has got worse.
teaching.audioText: In American English you might say that the situation has gotten worse, whereas a British speaker would say that it has got worse.

teaching.en: We usually visit my parents at the weekend, but our American friends would say on the weekend, or simply on weekends, for exactly the same plan.
teaching.es: Solemos visitar a mis padres el fin de semana, pero nuestros amigos estadounidenses dirían «on the weekend», o simplemente «on weekends», para el mismo plan.
teaching.explanationEs: At the weekend (RU) y on the weekend (EE. UU.) significan lo mismo; la preposición cambia.
segments: We usually visit my parents at the weekend, but our American friends would
say on the weekend, or simply on weekends, for exactly the same plan.
teaching.audioText: We usually visit my parents at the weekend, but our American friends would say on the weekend, or simply on weekends, for exactly the same plan.

teaching.en: The theatre in the centre of town has painted its doors a bright colour, but an American newspaper would print theater, center and color.
teaching.es: El teatro del centro de la ciudad ha pintado sus puertas de un color vivo, pero un periódico estadounidense escribiría «theater», «center» y «color».
teaching.explanationEs: Los finales -re y -our británicos pasan a -er y -or en EE. UU.
segments: The theatre in the centre of town has painted its doors a
bright colour, but an American newspaper would print theater, center and color.
teaching.audioText: The theatre in the centre of town has painted its doors a bright colour, but an American newspaper would print theater, center and color.

teaching.en: After travelling through Italy for a month, Sara learnt that the museum had cancelled its printed catalogue, and an American editor would write traveling, learned, canceled and catalog.
teaching.es: Tras un mes viajando por Italia, Sara se enteró de que el museo había cancelado su catálogo impreso, y un editor estadounidense escribiría «traveling», «learned», «canceled» y «catalog».
teaching.explanationEs: El inglés británico duplica la l final (travelling, cancelled); learnt es la forma británica de learned.
segments: After travelling through Italy for a month, Sara learnt that the museum had cancelled
its printed catalogue, and an American editor would write traveling, learned, canceled and catalog.
teaching.audioText: After travelling through Italy for a month, Sara learnt that the museum had cancelled its printed catalogue, and an American editor would write traveling, learned, canceled and catalog.

teaching.en: The team are meeting this afternoon whilst the manager is abroad, although an American speaker would more probably say that the team is meeting while the manager is away.
teaching.es: El equipo se reúne esta tarde mientras el jefe está en el extranjero, aunque un estadounidense diría más bien «the team is meeting while…».
teaching.explanationEs: En inglés británico un sustantivo colectivo puede llevar verbo plural (the team are); whilst es una variante más formal de while.
segments: The team are meeting this afternoon whilst the manager is abroad, although an American speaker
would more probably say that the team is meeting while the manager is away.
teaching.audioText: The team are meeting this afternoon whilst the manager is abroad, although an American speaker would more probably say that the team is meeting while the manager is away.

teaching.en: The key to consistent spelling is to choose one variety and keep to it: write colour and theatre, or color and theater, but never a mixture of both.
teaching.es: La clave de una ortografía coherente es elegir una variedad y mantenerla: escribe «colour» y «theatre», o «color» y «theater», pero nunca una mezcla de ambas.
teaching.explanationEs: La coherencia importa más que la variedad elegida.
segments: The key to consistent spelling is to choose one variety and keep to it:
write colour and theatre, or color and theater, but never a mixture of both.
teaching.audioText: The key to consistent spelling is to choose one variety and keep to it: write colour and theatre, or color and theater, but never a mixture of both.

prompt.es: Completa en inglés británico: «nuestro nuevo teatro en el centro de la ciudad».

answer.text: centre
accepted: centre

feedback.es: En una publicación británica se escribe centre, con -re, igual que theatre.

origin.text: A leaflet for British readers announces: 'Our new theatre in the city ___ opens this weekend, and tickets are already selling fast.'

prompt.es: Elige la frase escrita por completo en inglés americano.

choices.text: The team is travelling to the center on the weekend.
The team are traveling to the center at the weekend.
The team is traveling to the center on the weekend.

feedback.es: Solo esta frase combina traveling, center, on the weekend y the team is: todo americano.

hint.es: Busca a la vez una l, -er, la preposición on y el verbo singular.

prompt.es: Ordena en inglés británico: «El equipo trabaja mientras el jefe está fuera.»

answer.text: The team are working whilst the manager is abroad

feedback.es: Con the team are el equipo se ve como un grupo de personas, y whilst introduce una acción simultánea.

hint.es: El sustantivo colectivo lleva are en inglés británico.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada variante con la variedad o el rasgo que la describe.

feedback.es: Cada variante se asocia a una variedad: on the weekend y gotten son estadounidenses; at the weekend, learnt y the team are, británicas.

prompt.es: Escucha al narrador y elige qué diferencia nota entre él y sus amigos.

choices.text: They express the same ideas with slightly different forms.
They cannot understand him when he talks about the weather.
They laugh at his pronunciation of the word weekend.

feedback.es: El narrador compara formas distintas para la misma idea (gotten/got, on/at, is/are); no hay problemas de comprensión ni de pronunciación.

origin.audio: I have lived in Bristol for two years, and my British friends still tease me. I say that the weather has gotten worse, and they say that it has got worse. I promise to call on the weekend, and they answer at the weekend. Last week my manager told everyone that the team are ready, and I almost corrected her, because back home we would say the team is ready.

prompt.es: Reescribe en inglés americano la frase del estímulo.

answer.text: Sara has gotten tickets for the theater on the weekend.
accepted: Sara has gotten tickets for the theater on the weekend.
Sara has gotten tickets for the theater on weekends.
Sara has gotten tickets for the theater this weekend.
Sara has gotten tickets to the theater on the weekend.
Sara has gotten tickets to the theater on weekends.
Sara has gotten tickets to the theater this weekend.

feedback.es: En inglés americano: has gotten, theater y on the weekend sustituyen a has got, theatre y at the weekend.

origin.text: Sara has got tickets for the theatre at the weekend.

prompt.es: Escucha a la editora y elige qué le pidió a la autora del artículo.

choices.text: To switch to British spelling, because the article was for readers in Manchester.
To pick one set of forms and use it throughout.
To write the team are in every sentence, as British editors do.

feedback.es: Le pide elegir una forma y mantenerla; ni toca su ortografía ni le pide adaptarla a Mánchester ni fijar the team are en todas las frases.

origin.audio: I work as an editor in Manchester, and last week an American author sent me an article. I did not touch her spelling, because it was perfectly consistent: color, theater and traveling all appeared in the American form. What bothered me was not her variety but one paragraph where she wrote the team is and then the team are. So I simply asked her to choose one form and keep to it throughout.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué opinión deja ver la editora sobre las dos variedades.

choices.text: American spelling is fine, but only in articles for readers in the United States.
British forms are better, because her editor works in Manchester.
Both are fine if the writer stays consistent.

feedback.es: Respeta la ortografía americana sin pedir cambios y solo corrige la mezcla: para ella, lo que importa es la coherencia, no la variedad.

origin.audio: I work as an editor in Manchester, and last week an American author sent me an article. I did not touch her spelling, because it was perfectly consistent: color, theater and traveling all appeared in the American form. What bothered me was not her variety but one paragraph where she wrote the team is and then the team are. So I simply asked her to choose one form and keep to it throughout.

prompt.es: Completa en inglés americano: «Ha conseguido un asiento en el tren nocturno.»

answer.text: gotten
accepted: gotten

feedback.es: Gotten es el participio estadounidense de get con el sentido de conseguir.

origin.text: Sara's flight was delayed, but she says that the situation has already improved. In American English you would write that she has ___ a seat on the night train.

prompt.es: Lee el correo para un cliente de Londres. ¿Qué cambio mantiene su coherencia británica?

choices.text: Write centre instead of center.
Write color instead of colour.
Write the team is instead of the team are.

feedback.es: El resto del correo es británico (colour, catalogue, the team are): solo center rompe la coherencia y debe ser centre.

origin.text: Email to a British client: 'Our new colours have arrived, and the team are pleased. We will send the catalogue on Friday, and we hope you will visit our new center soon.'

prompt.es: Lee el párrafo. ¿Qué postura defiende la autora sobre las variedades?

choices.text: Learners should learn the American forms before the British ones.
Seeing both varieties helps learners worry less about mistakes.
Teachers should never mention spelling differences in class.

feedback.es: Sostiene que conocer ambas variedades quita el miedo a equivocarse; no defiende aprender solo una ni ocultar las diferencias.

origin.text: Some teachers insist that only one variety is correct, but in my experience students learn faster when they see both. A learner who notices that colour and color, or at the weekend and on the weekend, mean exactly the same thing stops fearing mistakes.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los organizadores han cancelado el concierto por la tormenta.»

answer.text: cancelled
accepted: cancelled

feedback.es: La ortografía británica duplica la l al añadir -ed: cancelled; en EE. UU. se escribe canceled.

origin.text: Sara is writing for a British newspaper and wants to keep British spelling throughout: 'The organisers have ___ the concert because of the storm.'

prompt.es: Ordena en inglés americano: «El equipo ha cancelado su viaje al centro el fin de semana.»

answer.text: The team has canceled its trip to the center on the weekend
accepted: The team has canceled its trip to the center on the weekend
On the weekend the team has canceled its trip to the center

feedback.es: Canceled, center y on the weekend son las formas americanas; con the team el verbo va en singular: has.

es: Comprender la idea principal, el lugar y una palabra regional en mensajes breves de hablantes de distintas variedades.

teaching.en: When you listen to an unfamiliar accent, focus on the gist first, because the topic and the place matter more than every single word.
teaching.es: Cuando escuchas un acento que no conoces, concéntrate primero en la idea general, porque el tema y el lugar importan más que cada palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Gist = idea general; acento no familiar = unfamiliar accent.
segments: When you listen to an unfamiliar accent, focus on the gist first,
because the topic and the place matter more than every single word.
teaching.audioText: When you listen to an unfamiliar accent, focus on the gist first, because the topic and the place matter more than every single word.

teaching.en: The voice message was recorded on a noisy platform, so I could barely make out the words, although the place names helped me follow the topic.
teaching.es: El mensaje de voz se grabó en un andén ruidoso, así que apenas distinguía las palabras, aunque los nombres de lugar me ayudaron a seguir el tema.
teaching.explanationEs: Make out + palabras/voz = conseguir oír o entender con dificultad.
segments: The voice message was recorded on a noisy platform, so I could barely
make out the words, although the place names helped me follow the topic.
teaching.audioText: The voice message was recorded on a noisy platform, so I could barely make out the words, although the place names helped me follow the topic.

teaching.en: An Australian friend invited us to a barbie, the local word for a barbecue, and warned that it would be the last one for a fortnight because the rain is coming.
teaching.es: Un amigo australiano nos invitó a una «barbie», la palabra local para barbacoa, y avisó de que sería la última durante dos semanas porque viene la lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: Barbie (australiano) = barbecue; fortnight = dos semanas (RU, Irlanda y Australia).
segments: An Australian friend invited us to a barbie, the local word for a barbecue, and warned
that it would be the last one for a fortnight because the rain is coming.
teaching.audioText: An Australian friend invited us to a barbie, the local word for a barbecue, and warned that it would be the last one for a fortnight because the rain is coming.

teaching.en: In Houston, in the southern United States, a waiter asked whether y'all were ready to order, while my British friend quietly checked his mobile under the table.
teaching.es: En Houston, en el sur de EE. UU., un mesero preguntó si «y'all» estaban listos para pedir, mientras mi amigo británico miraba discretamente su celular bajo la mesa.
teaching.explanationEs: Y'all (sur de EE. UU.) = ustedes, un grupo; mobile = teléfono celular en inglés británico.
segments: In Houston, in the southern United States, a waiter asked whether y'all were ready
to order, while my British friend quietly checked his mobile under the table.
teaching.audioText: In Houston, in the southern United States, a waiter asked whether y'all were ready to order, while my British friend quietly checked his mobile under the table.

teaching.en: A Glasgow bloke thanked the driver with a quick cheers, and a regional word like that can reveal more about a speaker than an accent does.
teaching.es: Un tipo de Glasgow dio las gracias al conductor con un rápido «cheers», y una palabra regional así puede revelar más sobre alguien que su acento.
teaching.explanationEs: Bloke = hombre (RU y Australia); cheers = gracias o adiós informal (RU).
segments: A Glasgow bloke thanked the driver with a quick cheers, and a regional
word like that can reveal more about a speaker than an accent does.
teaching.audioText: A Glasgow bloke thanked the driver with a quick cheers, and a regional word like that can reveal more about a speaker than an accent does.

teaching.en: To pick up on clues about where a speaker comes from, listen for regional words and for the speed and melody of the voice, not only the accent.
teaching.es: Para captar pistas sobre el origen de quien habla, escucha las palabras regionales y la velocidad y melodía de la voz, no solo el acento.
teaching.explanationEs: Pick up on = darse cuenta de algo sutil; las pistas son léxico, ritmo y entonación.
segments: To pick up on clues about where a speaker comes from, listen for regional
words and for the speed and melody of the voice, not only the accent.
teaching.audioText: To pick up on clues about where a speaker comes from, listen for regional words and for the speed and melody of the voice, not only the accent.

prompt.es: Según la transcripción, ¿qué palabra regional sitúa a Mia y qué significa?

choices.text: Y'all, which addresses a whole group in the southern United States.
Y'all, which is used in Australia to address a group of friends.
Y'all, which Americans use to address one person politely.

feedback.es: Y'all es la palabra regional de la transcripción: se dirige a un grupo y es típica del sur de EE. UU.; no es australiana ni se usa para una sola persona.

hint.es: Busca la palabra con la que Mia saluda a varias personas a la vez.

origin.text: Transcript: 'Hey y'all, it's Mia from Austin. The game starts at seven, so come early and bring a jacket, because the stadium gets cold after dark.'

origin.audio: In my travel podcast I always try to check who is listening. Last month a listener from Canada wrote to say that my tip about packing your trainers and a jumper in the boot of the car had confused half her group. So now I say things like, pack comfortable shoes and a warm top, and leave your bags in the car. Neutral words may sound a little boring, but nobody has to stop and ask.
